New notifications from the phone (app, title, text, icon) go to the paired computer while it\'s connected. Nothing goes through a cloud or is stored. Ongoing notifications (such as a player or background navigation) are skipped. From the computer you can reply to a message and dismiss a notification; dismissed on one device, it goes away on the other.

This is a separate permission: in Android settings choose “WindConnect: notifications on the computer”. Media access isn\'t enough and isn\'t used here. Android 15 may hide sensitive content (such as SMS codes); the computer then sees “Content hidden” or nothing.

The computer can read this phone\'s SMS and MMS threads in the “Messages” window. The content goes only directly to the paired computer, encrypted, and isn\'t saved to its disk. Contacts (optional) give names and photos instead of bare numbers.

On an incoming call the computer shows a notification with the number and contact name, with “Decline” and “Silence” buttons, plus a list of missed calls from the last week. The data goes only to the paired computer.

When you turn it on, Android asks for phone state, the call log, answering calls (declining from the computer) and contacts (names). Without this feature the computer still knows only that the phone is ringing (to pause music).
use wss:// (ws:// only on a local network)

When the phone and the computer aren\'t on the same network, the connection can go through a relay. The content is end-to-end encrypted. The relay\'s operator sees both devices\' IP addresses, their public keys, when they connect and how much data goes through, but not its content or the devices\' names. Turning it off ends a relayed connection at once.
